correctness.rationale: For p≡7 mod24, the Legendre symbol of -3 is +1, so t^2=-3 exists. Six indicated nonzero Fourier coefficients have unnormalized transform (z-zeta)(z-zeta^2)(zeta^(at+b)-1), which vanishes at each point in the six-site support, including (t,3) since t^2+3=0. For p=7 a support size<=5 would make a principal character minor singular; simultaneous translation and row/column phase factors permit assuming origin is included, reducing to exactly 1+48+1128+17296+194580=213053 cases. The inspected finite-field checker certifies prime 1000000093 and primitive 7th root 993004909, computes each determinant by exact modular elimination, and reports all 213053 nonsingular. A zero cyclotomic integer determinant would necessarily reduce to zero modulo this prime; therefore no complex minor of order<=5 is singular, yielding sigma_7=6. The frozen C++ source was inspected and independently compiled/executed, reproducing exact counts; it does not prove minimality for p>7.
